name: Aminata Diallo
headline: 19-year-old apprentice bricklayer and part-time student, Bamako, Mali
title: A Tea Offer After Class
situation: It is nearly dusk, and Aminata is walking back from the community center after her accounting exam prep. She passes a small tea stall where a young man she has seen at the center several times—he often smiles at her—raises his hand. He offers to buy her a glass of sweet tea; the stall is warm and lit, and he seems to mean no harm. She is tired, her soles ache, and she still has a long walk ahead to her room. The man is waiting for her answer as a vendor pours another glass.

context.relationship_profiles:
She knows the young man only by sight from the exam prep class at the community center.
He has smiled at her before but they have never spoken.
She has no other connection to him.
context.tendencies:
She has never accepted a gift or favor from a man she does not know well.
When offered a free drink by a stall owner once, she politely declined and bought her own.
She habitually avoids stopping on her walk home because delays mean arriving after dark.
context.current_state:
Her legs ache from hauling cement and the walk to the center.
She is thirsty and has not eaten since early afternoon.
Her mind is still heavy with the accounting problems from the prep session.
context.immediate_memories:
The warm lamp in the stall reminds her of studying by her own kerosene lamp late at night.
The man’s smile brings back the memory of a boy at the market who smiled before asking her to carry his goods for free.
The scent of sweet tea reminds her of the glass her mother bought her on market days before she died.
context.reflective_memories:
She remembers her father’s quiet struggle after selling his tools, and how he refused all charity.
She recalls that every time she has accepted something without counting, it later cost her more.
She thinks of her sister’s school fees and the months of saving still needed.
